answer.rationale: Memory c2 is the critical load-bearing claim: that the low-cost vendor can deliver at sharply lower cost with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing. This directly supports the only action that can meet the 18% cut within the 14-day window. Memory c6 (multi-year volume pricing with the incumbent) is noted but cannot be executed in one cycle within 14 days and would not meet the mandated cut alone. Memory c1 confirms the incumbent's stability, but the contract expires in 14 days with no auto-renew, making renewal contingent on renegotiation that may not close in time. Verification budget is spent on c2 because the switch is irreversible this cycle and any onboarding risk compounds against the 94% assembly-line utilization with zero buffer.
